name: Coolidge Scholarship
summary: A full-ride, merit-based scholarship for high school juniors who show academic excellence, service, humility and an interest in public policy. It covers tuition, room, board and fees for four years at any accredited U.S. college.
how_to_apply: Juniors apply online at coolidgescholars.org in the fall of junior year; all materials, including reference letters, are due by the December deadline.
amount_text: Full tuition, room, board and required fees for four years, plus a yearly book stipend
deadline_text: December 1, 2026 at 5:00 PM Pacific (for juniors starting college in fall 2028)
other_requirements: Must be a current high school junior who will start college full-time in fall 2028 (gap years and early graduation disqualify). Finalists interview in Vermont.

name: Profile in Courage Essay Contest
summary: A national essay contest for high school students who write about an elected official who showed political courage. Winners earn cash awards for college.
how_to_apply: Write a 700 to 1,000 word essay with at least five sources and submit it with the online registration form by the January deadline.
amount_text: $10,000 first place; $3,000 second; $1,000 for each of three finalists
deadline_text: January 11, 2027 at 11:59 PM Eastern
other_requirements: Open to U.S. students in grades 9-12 (public, private, home school) and U.S. citizens attending school overseas.

name: Voice of Democracy Scholarship Competition
summary: An audio-essay contest for high school students on a patriotic theme. Local, state and national winners earn scholarships, with a top national prize of $35,000.
how_to_apply: Record a short audio essay on the year's theme and turn it in with the entry form to a participating local VFW Post by October 31.
amount_text: Top national award $35,000; other national awards up to $21,000; state winners at least $1,000
deadline_text: October 31 each year (the 2026-27 deadline has passed; next one is October 31, 2027)
other_requirements: Enter through a local VFW Post.

name: Patriot's Pen Youth Essay Contest
summary: A patriotic essay contest for middle school students (grades 6-8). Winners earn cash awards, with $5,000 for the national first-place winner.
how_to_apply: Write a 300 to 400 word essay on the year's theme and turn it in with the entry form to a participating local VFW Post by October 31.
amount_text: $5,000 national first place; state winners at least $500
deadline_text: October 31 each year (the 2026-27 deadline has passed)
other_requirements: Grades 6-8 only. Enter through a local VFW Post.

name: American Legion National High School Oratorical Contest
summary: A speech contest about the U.S. Constitution for high school students. Winners advance from local to state to national rounds and earn college scholarships up to $25,000.
how_to_apply: Contact your local American Legion post or the Georgia department to enter the post-level contest, usually held in winter; state winners go to the national finals in May.
amount_text: $25,000 national winner; $22,500 second; $20,000 third; $2,000+ for each state winner at nationals
deadline_text: Local and state contests run in winter; state winners must be certified by April 5, 2027; national finals May 14-16, 2027
other_requirements: Must be under 20 and in grades 9-12. Speak in the state where you live or attend school.

name: Army ROTC High School Scholarship
summary: A merit scholarship for students who want to become Army officers. It pays college tuition and fees (or room and board) plus monthly and book allowances, in exchange for military service after college.
how_to_apply: Create an account and apply online starting in the summer before senior year; there are three review rounds, so applying early helps.
amount_text: Full tuition and fees or room and board, $420 a month, and $1,200 a year for books
deadline_text: Round 1 Oct 12, 2026; Round 2 Jan 18, 2027; Round 3 Mar 8, 2027 (must start by Mar 4, 2027)
other_requirements: Must take the SAT or ACT, pass an Army fitness test and meet body standards, and agree to serve as an Army officer (8-year obligation).

name: Navy ROTC National Scholarship
summary: A competitive merit scholarship for students who want to become Navy or Marine Corps officers. It pays tuition and fees plus a book stipend (or room and board) at participating colleges.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the NROTC application website; the application period runs from April to December, and all documents go through your Navy ROTC coordinator.
amount_text: Full tuition, educational fees, and a book stipend (or room and board)
deadline_text: Applications accepted April 1 to December 31; application website closes January 31
other_requirements: ACT minimum is 22 English and 21 Math (44 combined); SAT minimum 1100 (540 Math, 550 reading). Must be 17 by Sept 1 of the college start year. Must serve as an officer after graduating.

name: Air Force ROTC High School Scholarship
summary: A merit scholarship for students who want to become Air Force or Space Force officers. It pays college tuition plus a $900 yearly book stipend and a monthly allowance.
how_to_apply: After junior year, create an account and apply online between July 1 and December 11; you'll upload transcripts, test scores and a fitness assessment.
amount_text: Tuition (capped or uncapped), $900 a year for books, and $300-$500 a month
deadline_text: Application window July 1 to December 11, 2026 (for fall 2027 college entry)
other_requirements: Must pass a fitness assessment and military medical exam, and serve at least four years on active duty after college.

name: Gloria Barron Prize for Young Heroes
summary: Honors young people ages 8 to 18 who have started and led a service project that helps people, animals or the planet. Each winner gets $10,000 for college or their project.
how_to_apply: Complete a short pre-application online in winter, then a full application by mid-April.
amount_text: $10,000 per winner
deadline_text: Pre-application usually January to March 15; full application due April 15 (2027 dates not posted yet)
other_requirements: Ages 8-18 on April 15. Must be a U.S. or Canadian permanent legal resident with an SSN or tax ID. The project must be one you started and led, active within the past 12 months.

name: Breakthrough Junior Challenge
summary: A worldwide video contest for students ages 13 to 18 who explain a big idea in science or math. The winner receives a $250,000 college scholarship.
how_to_apply: Make a short video explaining a science or math concept and submit it online during the summer window, then review other students' videos.
amount_text: $250,000 college scholarship (plus prizes for the winner's teacher and school)
deadline_text: Entries usually open in May and close September 15 (2026 round closed; 2027 dates not posted yet)
other_requirements: Ages 13-18. Entries must be in English.

name: Junior Science and Humanities Symposium (JSHS)
sponsor: Department of Defense / Academy of Applied Science
summary: A research competition where high school students present original science, engineering or math research at regional and then national symposiums. Top presenters earn college scholarships.
how_to_apply: Contact your regional JSHS (find it on jshs.org) and submit a research paper by the regional deadline, usually in winter.
amount_text: Regional: $2,000 / $1,500 / $1,000; National: up to $12,000 per category winner (max $30,000 per student)
deadline_text: Regional symposiums are held in winter to early spring; check your region
other_requirements: Must have done original research. National scholarship renewals require a 3.0 college GPA and a STEM major.

name: eCYBERMISSION
summary: A free online STEM contest for teams of students in grades 6-9 who solve a problem in their community. State, regional and national winners earn U.S. savings bonds.
how_to_apply: Form a team of 2-4 students with an adult advisor, register by February 24, 2027, and submit your Mission Folder by March 3, 2027.
amount_text: U.S. savings bonds at state, regional and national levels
deadline_text: Register by February 24, 2027; Mission Folder due March 3, 2027
other_requirements: Rising 6th through 9th graders. Teams of 2-4 with an adult Team Advisor.

name: Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge
sponsor: Society for Science / Thermo Fisher Scientific
summary: The top national science and engineering competition for middle school students (grades 6-8). Students nominated from local science fairs compete for awards, with a top prize of $25,000.
how_to_apply: Compete at a Society-affiliated science fair; if nominated, complete the online application, usually due in early June.
amount_text: Top award $25,000; over $100,000 in total awards
deadline_text: 2026 application ran February 1 to June 10; 2027 dates not posted yet
other_requirements: Grades 6-8 in the U.S. Must be nominated by placing in the top 10% at an affiliated science fair.

name: 3M Young Scientist Challenge
summary: A video science contest for students in grades 5-8 who propose an invention that solves an everyday problem. The national winner receives $25,000 and a 3M mentorship.
how_to_apply: Submit a short video explaining your idea at YoungScientistLab.com; entries usually open in January and close in late April.
amount_text: $25,000 grand prize
deadline_text: 2026 entries closed April 30, 2026; the 2027 contest usually opens in January
other_requirements: Grades 5-8 only.

name: U.S. Stockholm Junior Water Prize
summary: A competition for high school students who have done a water-related science research project. State winners go to nationals, where the U.S. winner gets a $10,000 scholarship and a trip to Stockholm.
how_to_apply: Enter your water research paper online for your state competition (through a science fair or by self-nominating); state winners are named in early May.
amount_text: $10,000 scholarship for the U.S. national winner
deadline_text: State competitions run in spring; national finals in June
other_requirements: Must be at least 15 by August 1 of the competition year and have completed a water-related science project.

name: Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF)
summary: The world's largest pre-college science fair. High school students who win at affiliated local and state fairs compete for millions of dollars in awards and scholarships.
how_to_apply: Do a science or engineering research project and compete at a Society-affiliated regional or state science fair; top winners are sent to ISEF in May.
amount_text: Over $7 million in total awards, prizes and scholarships
deadline_text: ISEF 2027 is in May 2027 in Los Angeles; qualify through your regional/state fair in winter or spring
other_requirements: Must qualify by winning at a Society-affiliated science fair.

name: C-SPAN StudentCam Documentary Competition
summary: A national documentary contest for students in grades 6-12 who make a short video about a public policy issue. 150 prizes are awarded, with a $5,000 grand prize.
how_to_apply: Make a 5 to 6 minute documentary on the year's theme that includes C-SPAN clips, upload it, and complete the entry form by January 20, 2027.
amount_text: $5,000 grand prize; $3,000 first; $1,500 second; $750 third; $250 honorable mention
deadline_text: January 20, 2027 at 11:59 PM Pacific
other_requirements: Individuals or teams of 2-3. The 2027 theme is "Mr. Speaker, I Rise To..."

name: Washington Crossing Foundation National Scholarship
summary: Scholarships for high school seniors who plan a career in government service at the local, state or federal level. Winners attend an awards luncheon in Pennsylvania.
how_to_apply: Mail three copies of your packet (cover page, short essay on why you want a government career, counselor or principal letter, transcript, test scores and resume) postmarked by January 15, 2027.
deadline_text: Postmarked by January 15, 2027
other_requirements: Must plan a career in government service. Mail-in only (no email). Winners must attend the April 24, 2027 ceremony in Pennsylvania (travel paid).

name: Princeton Prize in Race Relations
summary: Recognizes high school students who have led volunteer work that advances racial equity or understanding in their school or community. Winners receive $2,500 and an invitation to a symposium at Princeton.
how_to_apply: Complete Part I of the online application and invite an adult supporter (not a relative) to complete Part II online.
amount_text: $2,500 cash award
deadline_text: Deadline for 2026-27 not yet posted; check the site
other_requirements: Must attend a U.S. school (including home school). The activity must be volunteer work you led within the past 12 months.

name: Blue Planet Awareness Contest (formerly Ocean Awareness Contest)
summary: A free art, writing, film and music contest for students ages 11 to 18 about environmental issues. Winners receive cash awards and scholarships.
how_to_apply: Create a piece in any category on the 2027 theme, "Nature of Truth," and submit it online with an adult sponsor's contact information by June 7, 2027.
amount_text: Cash awards and scholarships up to $1,000
deadline_text: June 7, 2027 at 11:59 PM Eastern
other_requirements: Ages 11-18; not yet in college.

name: Optimist International Essay Contest
summary: An essay contest for students under 19 run through local Optimist Clubs. Club winners advance to district contests for a $2,500 college scholarship.
how_to_apply: Write an essay on the year's topic (2026-27: "Finding My Voice in a World Full of Noise") and submit it to your local Optimist Club; email programs@optimist.org to find one.
amount_text: $2,500 district scholarship
deadline_text: Set by each local club; club contests are finished by early February
other_requirements: Must be under 19 on October 1 and not yet graduated from high school. Enter through the Optimist district where you live.

name: Carson Scholars Fund Scholarship
summary: Honors students in grades 4-11 with top grades who also serve their communities. Each winner receives $1,000 toward college, a medal and a trophy for their school.
how_to_apply: A teacher, counselor or principal must nominate you (one student per school); then you complete the application with a teacher recommendation and report card.
amount_text: $1,000 (invested for college)
deadline_text: Nominations usually close mid-December and applications mid-January (2025-26: Dec 17 and Jan 11)
other_requirements: Grades 4-11 only. Must be nominated by a school official. 3.75 GPA in core academic subjects. Must do community service beyond what is required.

name: Amazon Future Engineer Scholarship
summary: For high school seniors with financial need who plan to study computer science or a related field. Winners get up to $40,000 for college plus a paid Amazon internship.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the application window (sign up on the site for updates); the 2025-26 cycle has closed.
amount_text: Up to $10,000 a year (covers unmet need), plus a paid summer internship
deadline_text: Next cycle dates not posted; the 2025-26 window has closed
other_requirements: Must have taken a computer science course (or take an Amazon assessment) and plan a computer science-related bachelor's degree. Must be authorized to work in the U.S.

name: NHS Scholarship
summary: Scholarships for senior members of the National Honor Society, awarded for scholarship, service, leadership and character. About 600 students share $2 million.
how_to_apply: Log in to your NHS student account (verified by your chapter adviser) and submit the online application by November 20, 2026.
amount_text: $2 million total to 600 students
deadline_text: November 20, 2026 at 5:00 PM Eastern
other_requirements: Must be an active NHS member in good standing.

name: National FFA Scholarship Program
summary: One application gives FFA seniors a chance at many sponsor scholarships, worth nearly $2.5 million in total. Awards can be used for trade school, two-year or four-year college.
how_to_apply: Complete one online application (Kaleidoscope portal) between November 1, 2026 and January 14, 2027.
amount_text: Nearly $2.5 million in total awards
deadline_text: January 14, 2027 (opens November 1, 2026)
other_requirements: Must be an FFA member.

name: Boys & Girls Clubs Youth of the Year
summary: The top honor for Boys & Girls Club teens, recognizing leadership, service and academics. Winners move from Club to state, regional and national levels and earn scholarships.
how_to_apply: Talk to staff at your local Boys & Girls Club; members are chosen at the Club level first.
amount_text: $2,500 state winners; $20,000 regional winners; $50,000 National Youth of the Year
deadline_text: Selected at local Clubs each year; ask your Club for dates
other_requirements: Must be a Boys & Girls Club member.

name: mikeroweWORKS Work Ethic Scholarship
summary: Helps students train for skilled trades like construction, welding, HVAC, mechanics and some health careers. Awards pay toward short programs of two years or less.
how_to_apply: Sign the S.W.E.A.T. Pledge and apply online with a tuition bill from your program; applications are reviewed in four rounds a year.
amount_text: Varies (recent round: $3.5 million to 450 students)
deadline_text: Review rounds close April 30, June 30, August 30 and October 31
other_requirements: Must be a high school senior or graduate enrolling in an approved trade program of two years or less (not four-year degrees).

name: George S. and Stella M. Knight Essay Contest
sponsor: National Society Sons of the American Revolution (SAR)
summary: An essay contest for high school students about the American Revolution, the Declaration of Independence or the Constitution. Winners move from chapter to state to national levels.
how_to_apply: Write an 800 to 1,200 word essay and submit it through a local SAR chapter; in Georgia the deadline is December 1.
amount_text: Cash awards at chapter, state and national levels
deadline_text: Georgia deadline December 1 (other states mostly December 31)
other_requirements: U.S. citizens or legal residents. Contact your local SAR chapter's essay chair.

name: Stephen J. Brady Stop Hunger Scholarship
summary: For young people ages 5 to 25 who are fighting hunger in their communities. National winners get a $10,000 scholarship plus a $5,000 grant for their hunger charity.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the annual window, which runs August 20 to October 20.
amount_text: $10,000 scholarship plus $5,000 for a hunger-relief charity
deadline_text: Annually August 20 to October 20 (the 2026 window has closed)
other_requirements: Must be doing hands-on work to fight hunger.

name: Evans Scholarship
sponsor: Western Golf Association / Evans Scholars Foundation
summary: A full housing and tuition scholarship for golf caddies with strong grades, financial need and good character. Scholars attend partner universities, mostly in the Midwest.
how_to_apply: Apply online starting August 1 of senior year; school evaluations, transcript and caddie evaluation are due September 30, and the CSS Profile and FAFSA by October 15.
amount_text: Full tuition and housing
deadline_text: Applications open August 1 of senior year; materials due September 30 (class of 2027 window has passed)
other_requirements: Must have caddied regularly for at least two years and be sponsored by a golf club. B+ or better in college-prep courses. Must attend an Evans partner university.

name: Stokes Educational Scholarship Program
summary: For high school seniors planning to study computer science, engineering, cybersecurity, math or related fields. NSA pays up to $30,000 a year in tuition plus a salary, and you work for NSA after college.
how_to_apply: Apply through the NSA job listing (opens September 1) and email your resume, transcript, two recommendations, test scores and essay.
amount_text: Up to $30,000 a year for tuition and fees, plus year-round salary
deadline_text: Opens September 1 of senior year; closing date not posted (apply early)
other_requirements: Must be able to get a security clearance and agree to work for NSA after graduation (1.5 times the length of study).

name: SME Education Foundation Scholarships
summary: Scholarships for graduating seniors and college students studying technical fields that support manufacturing, such as engineering and industrial technology.
how_to_apply: Apply online between November 1 and February 1.
deadline_text: Applications accepted November 1 to February 1 each year
other_requirements: Must pursue an associate or bachelor's degree in a manufacturing-related technical field.

name: Doodle for Google
summary: An art contest for K-12 students to design a Google logo on a yearly theme. The national winner gets a $45,000 college scholarship and a technology package for their school.
how_to_apply: Create a Doodle on the year's theme and submit it online during the fall entry window.
amount_text: $45,000 scholarship for the national winner
deadline_text: 2025-26 contest ran October 15 to December 10, 2025; check for the next contest
other_requirements: Must attend a U.S. school (including home school).

name: ANS Incoming Freshman Scholarship
summary: Scholarships for students starting college who are interested in nuclear science and engineering.
how_to_apply: Apply online between November 1 and April 1; you don't need to be an ANS member to apply.
deadline_text: Applications open November 1; due April 1
other_requirements: Winners must join ANS before receiving the award.

name: ARRL Foundation Scholarship Program
summary: More than 170 scholarships for licensed amateur (ham) radio operators heading to college or trade school.
how_to_apply: Submit one online application during the fall; the last cycle closed December 30, 2025.
deadline_text: Usually closes around December 30
other_requirements: Must hold an active FCC amateur radio license.

name: DECA Scholarships
summary: Many sponsor scholarships for DECA members interested in business fields like marketing, finance, hospitality and entrepreneurship.
how_to_apply: Create an account on DECA's scholarship site, upload a transcript and three recommendations, and apply by January 11, 2027.
amount_text: $1,000 to $2,500 per award
deadline_text: January 11, 2027
other_requirements: Must be a current DECA member. Some awards have extra requirements.

name: PDK Educational Foundation Scholarships (Educators Rising)
summary: About 100 scholarships for future teachers, including high school seniors who are Educators Rising members.
how_to_apply: Apply online through PDK's Slayte portal (opens in January) with your transcript and one recommendation.
amount_text: $500 to $4,000; some renewable
deadline_text: Usually March 1
other_requirements: Must be a member of Educators Rising ($15 a year, waivers available), Pi Lambda Theta or PDK, and plan a career in education.

name: Samsung American Legion Scholarship
summary: For juniors attending American Legion Boys State or Auxiliary Girls State who are descendants of wartime veterans. Winners receive up to $10,000 for college.
how_to_apply: Apply online before the end of Day 1 of your Boys State or Girls State session.
deadline_text: Due on Day 1 of your Boys State / Girls State session (summer after junior year)
other_requirements: Must attend Boys State or Girls State and be a direct descendant of a U.S. veteran who served during a wartime period.

name: National Beta Scholarship
summary: Scholarships for senior members of the National Beta Club. Over $300,000 is awarded to 260 students each year.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application as an active senior Beta member by mid-January.
amount_text: 249 awards of $1,000, plus larger awards up to $20,000
deadline_text: Usually mid-January (2026 cycle closed January 15, 2026)
other_requirements: Must be an active 12th-grade Beta Club member.

name: JEA National High School Journalist of the Year
summary: Honors the top senior student journalist. State Journalist of the Year winners compete nationally for scholarships.
how_to_apply: Submit a portfolio to your state's Journalist of the Year contest; state winners apply nationally by March 15, 2027.
amount_text: $4,000 top winner; up to five finalists $1,200 each
deadline_text: National entries due March 15, 2027 (state deadlines are earlier)
other_requirements: Must win your state Journalist of the Year contest first. Your journalism adviser must be a JEA member.

name: Bennington Young Writers Awards
summary: A free writing contest for high school students in poetry, fiction and nonfiction. Winners earn cash prizes and big scholarships if they enroll at Bennington.
how_to_apply: Submit your piece online with a sponsoring teacher's approval between September 1 and November 1.
amount_text: $2,000 first place; $1,000 second; $500 third (plus Bennington tuition scholarships)
deadline_text: Submissions September 1 to November 1 each year (2026 contest closed)
other_requirements: Seniors must also submit a Common or Coalition App showing interest. Entries need a teacher or mentor sponsor.

name: Diamond Challenge
summary: A free business and social innovation pitch competition for teams of high school students. Top teams share over $100,000 in prizes.
how_to_apply: Form a team of 2 to 4 students and submit your business or social venture concept online by January 14, 2027.
amount_text: Over $100,000 prize pool
deadline_text: January 14, 2027
other_requirements: Teams of 2-4 high school students.

name: GE-Reagan Foundation Scholarship
summary: Rewards high school seniors who show leadership, drive, integrity and citizenship. Winners receive $10,000 a year for up to four years.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Kaleidoscope portal with activities, an essay and goals statement by January 7, 2027.
amount_text: $10,000 a year, renewable up to $40,000
deadline_text: January 7, 2027 at 3:00 PM Eastern

name: Jimmy Rane Foundation Scholarship
summary: Need-based scholarships for strong students from 26 states including Georgia. Awards are renewable for four years.
how_to_apply: Apply online starting December 1, 2026; applications are due February 5, 2027 and recommendations February 10, 2027.
amount_text: $500 to $6,000 a year, renewable for four years
deadline_text: February 5, 2027 (recommendations by February 10)
other_requirements: Must live in one of 26 eligible states (Georgia included). Not for students who will play college sports.

name: Toshiba/NSTA ExploraVision
sponsor: Toshiba and National Science Teaching Association
summary: A K-12 team science contest where students imagine a future technology. Members of top national teams each get up to a $10,000 savings bond.
how_to_apply: With a teacher coach, form a team of 2-4 students, research a technology idea, and register and submit by January 27, 2027.
amount_text: First place: $10,000 savings bond (or $5,000 cash/529) per student; second place: $5,000 bond
deadline_text: Registration closes January 27, 2027
other_requirements: Teams of 2-4 students with a teacher coach.

name: AIAA Roger W. Kahn Scholarship
sponsor: American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA)
summary: Scholarships for high school seniors with a strong interest in aerospace who plan an aerospace or STEM major.
how_to_apply: Join AIAA's free high school membership and apply online between September 21 and January 10.
amount_text: Up to four $10,000 scholarships
deadline_text: Applications September 21 to January 10
other_requirements: Must show aerospace interest through activities and hold a free AIAA high school membership.

name: Glenn Miller Scholarship Competition
summary: A music competition for high school seniors and college freshmen who plan to focus on music. Finalists perform in Iowa for vocal and instrumental scholarships.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application and recordings in spring (2026 deadline was April 20); finalists travel to Clarinda, Iowa.
amount_text: $10,000 first, $5,000 second, $3,000 third in each category
deadline_text: Usually mid-to-late April (2027 date not posted)
other_requirements: Finalists must travel to Clarinda, Iowa at their own cost.

name: American Welding Society Foundation Scholarships
summary: Millions in scholarships for students entering welding and related programs, from short certificates to two- and four-year degrees.
how_to_apply: Fill out one online application at scholarship.aws.org; it shows every scholarship you qualify for.
deadline_text: National, district and section scholarships due March 1; Welder Training Scholarship due November 30, 2026
other_requirements: Must be enrolled or about to enroll in a welding program (at least 50% welding coursework). Some awards need AWS membership (free for students) or U.S. citizenship.
